history.summary: The Veerabhadra Temple at Lepakshi was built in the 16th century by the brothers Virupanna Nayaka and Viranna, governors under the Vijayanagara Empire. A masterpiece of Vijayanagara (Dravidian) architecture entirely in granite, it is famous for its hanging pillar, the 27-ft monolithic Nandi, the Kalyana Mandapa, and well-preserved ceiling murals (one panel said to be among Asia's largest). Legend ties Lepakshi to the Ramayana: Jatayu fell here and Rama said 'Le Pakshi' ('rise, bird'). It is a centrally protected monument (ASI) and one of 108 Shiva Divya Kshetras. CSV town corrected from Anantapur to Lepakshi; district corrected from Anantapur to Sri Sathya Sai (district created in the 2022 bifurcation). Timings conflict across sources: most list 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM, one lists 5:00 AM - 12:30 PM and 4:00 PM - 8:30 PM (verify).

name: Veerabhadra Temple, Lepakshi
town_description: Lepakshi is a small village in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh, about 15 km east of Hindupur on the Karnataka border and 120 km north of Bengaluru. Its identity is almost entirely the 16th-century Veerabhadra temple complex; Ramayana legend says the wounded Jatayu fell here and Rama commanded 'Le Pakshi' (rise, bird), giving the village its name.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~100-120 km); taxi from the airport
travel.railway: Hindupur Railway Station (~15 km); then taxi or bus to Lepakshi
travel.road: 15 km east of Hindupur; well connected by road from Bengaluru (~120 km) and Anantapur; APSRTC buses and private taxis available
